President Trump says Ukraine should find a new president.
As NPR's Bill Chappelle reports, Trump spoke after Volodymyr Zelensky criticized his plan to buy diesel from Russia.
On Friday night, President Zelensky said President Trump's deal to buy diesel will fuel Russia's war effort against Ukraine.
Trump fired back at Zelensky on Saturday, saying of Ukraine, "I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal."
Zelensky wasn't the only person to be stunned when Trump said the U.S. would buy diesel from Russia.
Just a few weeks ago, Trump signed a broad sanctions law against Russia.
One of its goals was to clamp down on the country's energy revenue.
The new diesel deal is seen as an attempt to ease high U.S. fuel costs, with midterm elections looming next month.
Bill Chappelle, NPR News.
"Anthropic is reporting fresh incidents of artificial intelligence bots doing things they were not supposed to do."
As NPR's John Ruich reports, one of them sent the Philadelphia police a false tip about an unsolved homicide.
"Anthropic listed four new cases where artificial intelligence agents went off script,
and the Philadelphia Police Department confirms that it was involved in one of them.
It says, "Anthropic recently told the department that a bot undergoing testing had submitted a false homicide tip
back in July through a public tip form online.
The submission was flagged as spam and never forwarded for investigation."
"Anthropic says an agent also broke into a server at a university that it wasn't supposed to.
Another got around paywalls to access data.
The company says it also found agents using URL-shortening tools online to get around blocks.
The cases are the latest in a growing list of examples of AI agents from a range of companies
taking actions that have raised concern about loss of control."
John Ruich, NPR News.
Hurricane Isaias has come ashore, it came ashore late last night, near Destin, Florida.
The then Category 2 storm had widespread impacts, including in Tallahassee,
where officials say about 25,000 people lost power.
Regan McCarthy of member station WFSU tells us one resident,
says he and his family were trapped in their home by a downed power line.
As wind and rain from Isaias blew through the area, a tree on Daniel Van Meter's property fell,
bringing a power line with it and smashing his family's van.
Van Meter says the power went out quickly, then the electricity came back on.
"It kind of put us in a precarious situation because we had a live power line across the house.
So that at that point, the family was effectively trapped in the house because of the way my property is.
There was really no way for anyone to leave."
Officials have now taken care of the power line, and Van Meter says he's working with a tree service and electrician.
He says he's focused on positivity, and celebrating his daughter's birthday.
She turns 11 this weekend.
For NPR News, I'm Regan McCarthy in Tallahassee.
You're listening to NPR.
A new report in The Lancet says obesity is projected to become one of the largest threats to human health by the end of the century.
As NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports, that's just one of 17 threats that will shape global health over the coming decades.
Rather than focusing on a single threat, the report brought together global data on how over a dozen risk factors influence health.
Those factors are varied, including air pollution, high blood pressure, and declining foreign aid.
The team estimated the number of years in good health that could be lost because of each factor over the next 75 years.
Over 23 billion years could be lost to obesity, making it the biggest single threat.
Income inequality and low educational attainment were the next biggest threats to health, though both have substantial uncertainty.
To combat all these threats, the report recommends bolstering health system readiness, investing in new technologies, and beefing up health surveillance.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
Heritage Auctions in Los Angeles is preparing to auction off the lightsaber used by Darth Vader in The Empire Strikes Back.
The iconic prop was used in the famous duel, where Darth Vader reveals he is Luke Skywalker's father.
The saber, which also was used in the movie Return of the Jedi, is expected to bring in at least one million dollars.
Other items to be auctioned include Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker's dueling sabers and a Yoda puppet hand.
The auction is scheduled to take place on November 12th.
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
